clips.title: The story
paras: In Dun Morogh, Training the Beast brings young dwarven hunters to the end of their first trials. After learning to soothe and tame wild predators in the snowy crags, they travel to Ironforge to learn how to care for, train, and sustain an animal companion.

After taming large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod, young hunters finish their trial near Kharanos under Grif Wildheart’s watch. Taming a beast is only half the bond. Grif sends his pupils up the mountain pass to Ironforge, where they seek the Hall of Arms in the military district.

Belia Thundergranite teaches animal care in Ironforge’s Hall of Arms. Revered among the dwarven kingdom’s master animal trainers, she shows young hunters how to nourish and care for their pets, teach them new battlefield skills, and call their spirits back if they fall while defending their master. Her lessons help turn a frightened wild beast into a loyal partner.

Dwarven tradition calls for respect between hunter and beast, not subjugation. Belia reminds young hunters that an animal companion reflects the care it receives. Fed well, respected, and properly trained, a beast will fight loyally against troggs, frost trolls, and any threat to Khaz Modan.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Friend, ya now have the power to tame a pet, but you must also gain the skills ta train it.

Travel to Ironforge and find the Hall of Arms. There you must speak to one of our most revered animal trainers, Belia Thundergranite. She'll give ya the power to train your new pet, so get goin', friend!
Belia is a friendly sort; you should have no problems gaining her approval. Good luck, friend.

clips.title: Completion
paras: A new recruit, eh? You're on your way to becoming a great adventurer, I see.

Yes, I can bestow you with the skills you need to train and guide your pet. Not only will you be able to teach your pet new abilities, you will now be able to feed your pet, as well as revive it, should it fall in battle.
Remember that the key to getting the most from your new pet is to respect it and treat it well. In turn, your pet will be your most loyal friend.
